faces.f:
"Even if you battle unseen, even if there is no one to witness your sacrifice—strike! Strike true. Strike from the heart. Let that be your legacy."
—Shiko
"Gravity is just a suggestion."

"She huffs like she's Queen Hellkite of the Scour, but we've been together for many journeys and she's never let me down."
—Mandakh, Mardu scout

"Khan Alesha ensured our survival. Now we will forge our future."
—Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
Too late, the elders realized the young prodigies shared a love of adventure and mischief.
"Sky and Ember, guide my blade!"
Elspeth saw their capture as an inconvenience, costing them precious time. Narset saw it as an opportunity to recruit allies to their cause.

"So, these dragons intend to also manifest through a sandstorm? I take some offense to that."
—Felothar, khan of the Abzan
The Abzan forces rallied to the call, driving back Sarkhan's feral dragon horde.

"Come crackling spear, come beating wing!
Come cavalier, come taut bowstring!"

"I trust Narset. I do not trust those she keeps counsel with."
—Kotis, the Fangkeeper
Temur scouts reported the arrival of unwanted visitors, and the whisperers ensured a chilling welcome.
"This can't be right. I should cross-reference with the archives immediately."
Asham discovered it was impossible to learn if he thought he already knew everything.

"I know leaving your old life was no easy choice. Welcome, Novice Sardul."
—Elsha
The sequence of chimes rang out a specific alarm: dragonstorm, half a day, southwest.

"There is no better way to measure a person's true character than to let them think they're above you."
—Master Xian

"Even dragons avoid Glintglaze Lake in this season. Which of you youngsters can tell me why?"
—Teacher Eliam

"Fish are like any other crop or flock. They must be carefully tended and never overharvested."
—Nasath, Kishla fisher

faces.f: Since the reestablishment of Highspire Monastery, its favored fighting styles have also resurged in popularity.

"Beware dragonstorms that strike from the sea. Their size always disguises their force."
—Narset
"Oh, I can absolutely verify its authenticity," chuckled Sarnai. "I was there when it was made."
Elementals conjured by Temur mages are forever watchful and swift.
Temur mages are experts at channeling elemental energy, shaping it into familiar forms from the world around them.
"The Meditation Realm is a willful puzzle. Seek, and it will impede. Wait, and it will permit passage."
Whisperers are conduits to the spirits of the land. They provide healing, guidance, and support to the Temur people.
In the Endless Song, Temur's whisperers hear spirits murmur of the past, present, and future.
"You say you come in peace. That you come here at all is an act of war."
"Our greatest teachers are those which the natural world has so thoroughly refined."

"Yes, yes, very good. However, I believe you were supposed to be working on your sword techniques?"
—Taigam
The Kin-Trees rediscovered after Dromoka's fall are tended by carefully chosen wardens.

"Eat you? Of course she won't. Pherah's got better taste than that."
—Visk, Qarsi Palace caretaker

"When an alliance outlasts its usefulness it's best to end it quickly."
—Heng, Sultai ambassador

"Do not test the mandrill. He knows a thief when he sees one."
—Notice posted at Lu Fen's apothecary
"If I die today, I will ensure my death is worthy of legend."

"Who are you to defy me? In my time, the sibsig knew their place."
—Sidisi, to Nishang
With the rising waters, bloodflies were found far from their usual swamps.

"Sing for us when we depart for battle, and sing for us if we fail to return."
—Mardu parting

"To escape Teval's justice, one must have a better plan than 'run away.'"
—Kotis, the Fangkeeper
"It's a pity to hoard life essence in a form so weak. Give it to me."
She's eager to start a new winning streak.
"Thank the ancestors. A few more weeks, and we would have discovered nothing but dead wood and lost kin."
"Welcome," the spirits of House Emesh whispered to Cemal. "Welcome, newest sprout of our Kin-Tree."

"Evil wears many faces. Keep your windows closed at night, or it might wear yours."
—Sultai warning
Dariya's first mistake was thinking they could short the Mardu trader on a deal. Their last was not considering the trader would bring backup.
"There's a new sinkhole, seven leagues east. I'll take Scratchy."
"Once flesh, now gold and jade. Once dead, now alive again. Once respected, now honored beyond imagination."
As the rebels breached Qarsi Palace, she realized her time in power was at its end.
Vast sinkholes in the Shifting Wastes revealed long-buried structures—and long-buried dangers.
As Sultai blades threatened Qatros city walls, Mehtma of House Fenzala turned her weapons on her political rivals.

"Unless you actually see my spirit join the Kin-Tree, never assume me so unprofessional as to die on the job."
—Ezcul of House Zanhar
Abzan spirits bereft of a Kin-Tree are condemned to a restless existence. Absent the purpose of family connection, many grow angry and violent.
Mardu war shrieks ensure their enemies are defeated before the battle even starts.

"'Victory is survival' is the tenet that guides us. My love, know that I will always ensure your survivial."
—Duvir, Mardu warrior, final letter
"Our khan would grant you clemency. She is naive. And unfortunately for you, she is also not here."
"Arrows? Ha! Wood and feather? Toys!"

"Let the dragonstorms rage. Let what seeks sustenance feed. Let Tarkir be what it was always meant to be."
—Sarkhan
He regained balance while his opponent regained consciousness.
The brushfires of Cori Mountain take on a life all their own.
The power of the dragonstorms transformed not only the land but many of the creatures within it.
A master of the Whirling Blade technique, he did not hesitate to leap to the monastery's defense.
"It isn't about expression or results. Doing the thing is itself the point."
With a swift motion Narset struck Sarkhan down. She would not let his fevered dreams of draconic dominance come to fruition. Not after all she had done to free Tarkir.
Mardu lightning rods disperse the energy of dragonstorms—or whatever happens to be touching the rods.

"The scouts should have been back hours ago. They might be in trouble. I'm sending Kyra."
—Eshki Dragonclaw
In this year's Lightning Proving, Paala reclaimed her confidence and her place in the Mardu.
"From Alesha to Zurgo, all Mardu khans started right here. At the front lines."

"An arrow alone can't fell a dragon, but an added bolt of lightning brings it tumbling to the ground."
—Balur, Mardu warrior
Dragons of Tarkir are born fully formed, roars blending with the storms as a single, inseparable voice.

"If you see a yeti of Qadat, then it has surely already seen you. And if you are within sight, you are within range."
—Nitula, Temur hunter
"Help the villagers to safety! I will hold the gate!"

"Fire is only as precise as your control over it."
—Danfeng, Jeskai mage
They're just as renowned for their banter as they are for their tactical teamwork.
Zurgo valued those who took initiative.

Community is strength.
—Tenet of the Decree of Thunder
"There has to be a faster route through Sagu Jungle. Give me a week."
"Sokran is no mere bear. She is friend, family, and confidante—and more intelligent than some of my blood relatives."
Dusan boxing matches allow contestants no weapons, no allies, and no excuses.

"Some days, you wish you were fighting a dragon."
—Eshki Dragonclaw
During Dromoka's reign, Qatros Karst City was a haven for the Abzan rebellion. Its current residents have not lost their proficiency against their former foes.
Created by a sudden sinking, Dusyut Forest attracts earthcarvers eager to explore its mysteries and test their magic.

"The war chargers seem restless. Let them out to play."
—Ermaz, Abzan border guard
With an echoing crash the effigy fell, the symbol of Atarka's tyranny expunged from Temur lands.
Abzan soldiers know they never enter battle alone.
An exceptional bout during the Zenith celebration will be noted by Temur elders and result in recruitment for higher ranks.
The bushwhacker's machete glanced off the root with a sickening crack. Slowly, the entire undergrowth turned to face him.
In the aftermath of war, Temur mages nurtured the land back to its former vitality.
The greatest honor a Sultai can receive is to be returned to the realm of the living.

Like talking to a grokmaul
—Tarkir expression meaning "a failure of diplomacy"
With Taigam whispering encouragement in his ear, Sarkhan threw aside his misgivings. The ritual would return him to his former glory. All he needed was a dragon's heart.
"Now I wonder . . . will anyone come to protect *you*?"
Many Sultai villages are protected by naga who weave magics to bless or curse as needed.
"I've spent my life feeding Atarka's desire and hungers. It's time to see to my own."
The Abzan pride themselves on the safety of their roads. To reject their escorts invites storm and sorrow.
Every part of every plant is useful—for food, for medicine, and for ceremonies.
There are those who developed peculiar tastes after generations of dining upon the remains of interclan rivalry.

"Dragons working alongside the Abzan, not as overlords but as equals. It feels like a dream."
—Anafenza
The Temur celebrate the end of the Unbroken Night with stories, dances, and feasts. They gather to witness the first light of dawn as the land sings in harmony.

faces.f: In power, in hunger, in cruelty—insatiable.
The essence of Tarkir was shaped into draconic embodiments of the re-formed clans.
Zhao had resolved to hold the bridge, defending the village behind him. But the villagers decided Zhao would not stand alone.

"You need not mourn. Their life essence has returned to the earth, where it will eventually bloom into a new form."
—Kotis, the Fangkeeper

A small shock to save a life, a large one to take it away.
—Mardu healer's adage
Some had doubted the whisperers' choice of Eshki for Dragonclaw. None did so after witnessing her in battle.
"The Twice Whisperer heals. The Dragonclaw protects. Together, we will rebuild the Temur."
"Through perennation, we stand together, families—ancestor and kin─united as one clan! Abzan!"
"A flurry of fists doesn't impress you? Perhaps if they're on fire?"
Differing philosophies were debated by bloodshed.
The Sultai approach was silent. The Temur response was deafening.
"The fishers were probably exaggerating the size of the crocodile they spotted, but maybe they weren't. Let's check it out."

"Life is full of tough calls. We honor the dead today to make better decisions tomorrow."
—Uruna, Mardu lieutenant
"I agreed to return and aid the Sultai. My friends here agreed to return and aid me."

"We came seeking a challenge. It seems we must continue searching."
—Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
Elegance. Precision. Grace. Qualities that must be practiced in writing as well as combat.

"No one of us could have built all this alone. A clan, a school, hope for the future. Thank you all."
—Narset, to Shiko, Taigam, and Elsha
Like clouds and snow, Jeskai dragons prefer to drift among the monastery's highest spires.
As the Temur returned to Karakyk during the chill of winter, some shadows overhead were a blessing rather than a threat.

"For his crimes—burn his blood and cut him from his ancestors. Perennation is only for family."
—Dictate of House Mevak in the banishment of Oret
"Rising waters have flooded many old places from the dragon's rule. I do not miss them."
Some paths through Gurmag Swamp are deserted for good reason.
They've attained a level of synchronicity beyond what's possible in a single lifetime.
Gvar carved his way through the Ancestral Maelstrom, seeking to restore the withered Kin-Tree and soothe the raging spirits.
Lanniao soared from Highspire Monastery all throughout Tarkir, carrying messages for monks and villagers alike.
"Each step we take is a decision that changes the course of our futures. We must be careful where we tread."
Scales streaked with lightning, trailing thunder in his wake, Neriv is the living banner around which the Mardu rally.
The Abzan believe in perennation—death is not only an end, but a return to the beginning.
"You know you shouldn't and the Sultai forbid you. But you can't resist the temptation, can you?"

faces.f: "Dried durian from the Marang River Valley! Candied cherries from the slopes of Cori! Genuine dragon scale cookware!"

faces.f: Slowly, the clans have begun to recover and adapt long-forgotten tactics.
To ensure a fair competition, the Great Assemblage's war shriek contest has two divisions: dragons, and everyone else.
When called to the land's defense, all come to protect their shared home. It's why many of the Temur use "family" and "herd" interchangeably.

"He just kind of followed me home one day. I mean, could you say no to this face?"
—Karasi, Mistrise provisioner
"As you act, so shall you be judged."

faces.f: She keeps watch for dragonstorms and rival clans alike. For dragons, she raises an alarm. For thieves, her blade.
"Hear me, Mardu! Our freedom is only beginning!"
The draconic power that flowed out from the dragonstorms imbued the landscape with draconic features—scales, claws, and appetites.
It's as if the metal itself rages.
Jeskai scholars fashioned devices to forecast the behavior of the dragonstorms.
Its eternal glow lights the way for weary travelers through the misty heights surrounding Pearl Lake.
Set in motion by artificers long forgotten, it remained loyal through the ages to the occupants of Kheru City.

"Rage. Greed. Arrogance. People only accuse dragons of what they fear in themselves."
—Sarkhan
Against dragonlords, khans, and Ugin himself, the golem survived. Original purpose forgotten, it awaits orders that will never come, from a world that has moved on without it.

"These caves hide beasts above and below their waters. For safe passage, the Sultai agree a small cargo trade is fair for risking our necks."
—Samor, Mardu border guard

"It's rare to see Temur so far from their own lands. I see no reason to interfere, but keep an eye on them nonetheless."
—Hamza of House Fenzala
Every spire is a physical dedication to the Way.

"I ask only that the winds return you to me as swiftly as they bear you and the Storm Crane away."
—Samthar, Sultai merchant, to Jialing, Jeskai monk
Dragonstorm chasers are not deterred by danger—they claim there is nothing like witnessing the land embracing the power of a storm.
With a warm fire and a fresh catch, Temur hunters find respite in even the coldest climates.
Long-standing disagreements between the Sultai and Abzan about how to honor their dead have led to rare but fierce skirmishes.
Built on a fumarole field, the village is a refuge of warmth amid the ice of the Qal Sisma mountains.
Through sun and storm, across steppe and swamp, Storm Crane Monastery flies wherever aid is needed.

"The Mardu breathe life into what was lost under the dragonlords. If the Abzan are upset, it should be at themselves."
—Tersa Lightshatter

"The people must know that the former seat of their oppression is cleansed. Throw open Qarsi's gates and let them see for themselves."
—Kotis, the Fangkeeper

"We may fight the Temur when territory demands it, but we've no desire to profane their sacred places."
—Taklai, Mardu convoy

"The most important part of a stronghold isn't its armaments or its walls. It's the reason people have to defend it."
—Gvar Barzeel, krumar captain
By the codes of Mardu and Abzan alike, both sides allowed their enemies time to grieve after a battle.
When spring melted the snow, fishers downstream of the Qadat Fire Rim learned of conflict between Temur and Jeskai from the gruesome flotsam.
By morning the only evidence of conflict between Temur hunters and Sultai scouts were abandoned banners in the freshly fallen snow.

"Abzan vintages are nice, but the sorghum wine made in Riverwheel Village is beyond compare."
—Iramaz, Abzan trader
The Mardu are centered in the present. The Jeskai look to the future. But both know when the time for talking is past.
When caught in a dragonstorm, Mardu and Abzan scouts have no choice but to ride together.
In every biome of Tarkir, the storms spew forth dragons well suited to dominate.
Some believe dragonstorms to be the combined dregs of the vanquished dragonlords' fury.
It gulps from the lava flow to spew gouts of molten rock upon its prey.
Some dragonstorms pass without a trace. Others can conquer worlds.
Dragonstorms are a dragon's first natural habitat. They rarely have any issues navigating the howling energies to come to the Abzan's aid.
The Stormnexus Ritual brought forth draconic protectors, but unleashed the chaos of storms.
The most curious and contemplative dragons gravitate towards Shiko and the scholars of the Jeskai.
Only Temur whisperers are allowed in the Dragon's Throat. All others must justify their presence to the valley's guardian.
"For the Mardu, the shelter of my wings; for our foes, the searing heat of lightning."

"When we first saw her exulting in the storm's thunder, we knew she belonged with us."
—Tersa Lightshatter
Dragon scholars flock to understand the innumerable species across Tarkir, but the question of "What is a dragon?" gets more difficult to answer every day.
Dragon's scales to adorn the hilt, dragon's bones to polish the blade, and dragon's breath to kindle its edge.
The essence of dragonfire has permeated Tarkir's landscapes since time immemorial.

Silumgar's remnants drown, a new Sultai rises.
There is always an influx of visiting Temur families when the geothermal vents are most active.
The dragon's roar silenced all challengers, yet it was only an echo of Ugin's power.
Ugin and the dragonstorms of Tarkir are intrinsically linked. With his death they weakened. With his life they raged. But even the Spirit Dragon does not hold them fully under his sway.

"Some days, you wish you were fighting an Eldrazi."
—Ugin

"Life ensures death. Death ensures life. Yet always I remain. Perhaps an abiding harvest needs an ageless shepherd."
—Ugin
With no dragonlord to hold her back, she was free to learn every secret Ugin left behind.
Slowly, with or without Ugin's help, the clans are recovering and adapting long-forgotten tactics.

"Evil wears many faces. Keep your windows closed at night, or it might wear yours."
—Sultai warning

"Dawn-kissed, he nourishes the golden grain."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet

"The archon fell like a star from the sky, meeting the rising sun at the horizon's edge."
—*The Cosmogony*

The Champion reached for a stone, and Heliod placed the sun into her hand.
—*The Theriad*

faces.f:
"Gazing at the unicorn, I felt closer to the majesty of Nyx than I ever had before."
—Oineus, traveling merchant
"In every one of you I see a hero's heart."
Is there a greater promise than the glory of the sunrise?
Those whose lives were uninspired are doomed to the wretched tedium of Phylias in death.
Death turned admirable conviction into pointless intransigence.

faces.f: "The promise of victory fills my heart. There is no room for fear."
An infinite journey in an infinitesimal time.
"We are bearers of the ancient light, keepers of sun-crowned Heliod's blessings. Fight, and the light will protect you!"
"I bring a dawn that no night can follow."
Leonin fight for neither god nor polis; their loyalty is to their pride.
To tame a griffin is to ride into legend.
"You are loved, child."

"Charge bravely. Fight selflessly. Act honorably. Iroas will watch over you."
—Verenis, priest of Iroas
"Our stories are full of ancient wisdom; they tell us who we are."
Leonin band together in the Underworld, taking solace in their strength until, at last, both pride and self are forgotten.

"Storms drove them westward to Ketaphos; wide plains shimmered in starlight.
Centaurs greeted them, offering gold-hued apples and grain-cakes."
—*The Callapheia*
"My time will come, when every soul will bask in my glory and obey my law."
Every soldier has a place to stand and a role to play.
Every footstep is a prayer, every road a temple.
"Zeal is the sharpest blade, and piety the strongest shield."

"The time has come for us to throw off the chains of tyrannical gods and antiquated superstitions."
—Tikaia, disciple of Uremides

"To provoke the mountain is to invite the avalanche."
—Perisophia the philosopher
When the gods go to war, mortals pay the highest price.
Chosen by Heliod, Daxos approached the pegasus without fear, and rode it without saddle or reins.
"I like to think Kytheon keeps watch over all of us."

"The first griffins were made by the gods to capture falling stars; they were given the keenest eyes and the swiftest wings, and sent to keep watch above the clouds."
—*The Cosmogony*
Not even death can quench a hero's inner fire.
"Why would I ever want to look away?"
The oracles of Meletis foresaw neither its rise from the depths nor the destruction it would leave in its wake.
Those who do not learn from their mistakes are bound to relive them.

"A great wave crashed, and a mighty wind blew out the stars."
—*The Cosmogony*
"And what did Erekastos teach us is the nature of the soul?"
The greatest minds in Meletis study under the masters at the Dekatia, a renowned school of magic and philosophy.

"Freedom lies in accepting a single path."
—Nyklos, Meletian philosopher
Tycthis's military career was a flop.

faces.f: Alythos sat and stared blankly out over the glassy oceans of Nerono, trying in vain to remember what he knew he had forgotten.

"Wave-borne, he watches over secrets of the shore."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet

"Storm-tossed and broken, Callaphe cried out to deep-dwelling Thassa.
Tritons came swiftly to save her, bringing her north to the Lindus."
—*The Callapheia*
"My time will come, when the rising tide will surge above the tallest mountain."

"Take your place among the stars."
—Kruphix, god of horizons
"Once you see past the veil we call 'reality,' altering your own shape is elementary."

"As the storm waves crushed my sailors, I cried out to Thassa. The next time I saw them, hard shells encased them, and they swam away to safety."
—Siona, captain of the *Pyleas*
"I see destruction, suffering, and one tormented glimmer of hope."
Instead of performing their daily devotions, Heliod's acolytes spent the morning picking strands of kelp off the altar.
It swims upon the winds and soars through the waves.
It eats the things that eat the things that are drawn to the light.
Normally, a cerberus sleeps one head at a time.
Cities offer tribute to Ephara and carve her image into their walls, imploring her to protect them from the dangers of the wild.
Starfish are its favorite prey.
When memory is torment, oblivion is bliss.
"I bring a flood that nothing can withstand."
A sip of recollection, an ocean of regrets.
Even in their mountain fortresses, the Akroans have learned not to anger Thassa.
Thassa's favor followed him to the Underworld. Even the waves of Nerono obeyed his will.
"You can no more stop me than you can halt the tide."

"May the skies be clear of gales and gulls."
—Meletian prayer
Tritons search for omens in its wake.
"No, no, and ... no."
"As the future slips its way into the present, it ceases to be my concern."
The sharp memory of Daxos's death stabbed into Elspeth's soul.

"Sing, beauty. Sing for death, and for the dead."
—Ashiok
"Some aspire to be mighty like the lion or the hydra. I am the parasite that feeds on them all."
Wherever it walks, famine follows behind.
In bleak Tizerus, all hope crumbles in your grasp.
The death of the party.
The more you struggle against death, the tighter its grip becomes.

"Kroxa devours what he may—not for sustenance or pleasure, but because it is his nature. He is unending hunger given form."
—Klothys, god of destiny

faces.f:
"Evil flourishes where ignorance thrives."
—Perisophia the philosopher
"I bring a death none can escape."
The Underworld erodes memory, identity, and eventually the physical form, leaving only crumbling statues called misera—hollow monuments to mortal futility.
One spiny tree with bitter fruit grows in the realm of Tizerus, outside the palace of Erebos.
Funerary masks help the newly dead resist the erosion of memory and identity in the Underworld.
The Returned retain no memory of their identities, but sometimes they mindlessly attempt familiar tasks.
From the echoes of a violent life, a terrible foe is born.

"How many more will die before you accept your fate?"
—Erebos, god of the dead

"Grief-struck, she weeps for each mortal's final death."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet
As a mortal, Phenax was the first to escape the Underworld. As a god, he brings his pawns along the same dark path.
Caught between life and death, between land and sea, between thought and oblivion.
Those caught attempting to escape the Underworld spend the rest of their existence trapped in the Mire of Punishment.
Rage-crowned Mogis swiftly rewards the virtue of brutality.

"Callaphe guided them into the
darkness of Hetos, the bleak mire;
Blood-horned minotaurs circled them,
axes aglimmer in shadow."
—*The Callapheia*
"My time will come, when life's frantic striving will fade into the boundless quiet of death."
"If you will not pour your drink out for me, I shall pour mine out for you."
The fury of the slaughter god Mogis burns within him.
Desecrating the dead is a convenient way for harpies to expand their foul collections.
"We offer to Mogis the blood of the weak, and in return he makes us strong."
"I don't know if the gods watch over their temples, but I figure it's best to be stealthy just in case."
Phenax is generous with gifts and unforgiving of debts.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I, II — Mill three cards. Then you may exile a creature or enchantment card from your graveyard. If you do, create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token.
III — You gain X life and scry X, where X is the number of Zombies you control.

faces.f: Dreams are just one more form of torment.
"Many have sought snake-twined Pharika's panacea. Do you wish to share their fate?"

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Gain control of target creature for as long as this Saga remains on the battlefield.
II — Until your next turn, creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able.
III — Each tapped creature deals damage to itself equal to its power.

faces.f: "It's not enough to surprise your opponent. You have to delight the crowd as well."
It's a small step from revel to bloodbath.

"Renata was mesmerized by the satyr's dance of gleeful indifference, of reckless grace and bright disaster."
—Luphea of Setessa, *Histories*
Magic is the true artist's medium.
Purphoros forged the manticore's tail from bronze, its teeth from silver, and its heart from hate.
"Not even death can catch me now!"

"Everything will be put back in its proper place."
—Klothys, god of destiny
Those who fought without honor in life are taken to Agonas and doomed to fight forever in its arenas.

"A cyclops thinks slowly but strikes quickly. Try to keep it thinking."
—Brigone, soldier of Meletis
Klothys set out to mend the destiny of Theros, her fury guiding every stitch.
Winners of the Iroan Games are forever remembered as heroes of their people.
Brashness is close enough to bravery.
"Feast, for your next meal may be your last!"
The flamespeakers of Akros live passionately, devoted to Purphoros and the cycle of destructive creation.

"Renata launched a dozen arrows into the minotaur's thick hide, but the monster didn't slow its charge. The fury of Mogis was upon it."
—Luphea of Setessa, *Histories*
The blessing is not the strength itself, but the knowledge of how to use it.
To some satyrs, only blasphemy is sacred.

"One-eyed and frightful, the cyclops
lifted a boulder and hurled it
seaward from cliff's edge, shattering
masts and scattering sailors."
—*The Callapheia*
"My time will come, when all the world will be reforged in the fires of my invention."

"Flame-wrapped, she dances a burning swath amid the clouds."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet
Mogis can fan a small flame of resentment into an inferno of madness.
"I bring a fire to recast all the world."
It's hard to keep a satyr down, even in the Underworld.
The minotaur polis of Skophos boasts grand temples to the god of slaughter.
To a satyr, a stampede is just another kind of revelry.
Distant thunder rumbled, a dread forewarning of Keranos's displeasure.
"Right now, in these first moments of creation, it is simultaneously nothing and everything."

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after IV.)
I, II, III — Until end of turn, target creature gains trample and gets +X/+0, where X is the number of lore counters on this Saga.
IV — Target creature you control fights up to one target creature you don't control. (Each deals damage equal to its power to the other.)

faces.f: The Underworld is anything but a resting place.
Bright flames quell the darkest nightmares.
Her webs, spun from her own hair, reach from Nyx to the mortal world and even into the Underworld.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Each player mills three cards.
II — Exile up to two target cards from graveyards. For each creature card exiled this way, you gain 1 life.
III — Return target creature or land card from your graveyard to your hand.

faces.f:
"Vine-wreathed, he nurtures life among the dead."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after IV.)
I — Create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.
II — Put three +1/+1 counters on target creature you control.
III — If you control a creature with power 4 or greater, draw two cards.
IV — Create a Gold token. (It's an artifact with "Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.")

faces.f: The Nessian Wood is never without defenders.
The scouts of Hyrax Tower keep watch at the edge of Setessan territory, protecting the polis from inhuman monsters and enemy armies.
Those who die as heroes are permitted to dwell in Ilysia, a protected realm of the Underworld as tranquil and vibrant as the rest is bleak.
Nylea appeared amid the howl of a hundred beasts.
The god of destiny grants her followers vision deeper than sight.

"I see... elk? And lion? And... teeth! A lot of teeth!"
—Teraklos of Meletis

"Be fearless, for a furious rebirth awaits you."
—Nylea, god of the hunt
Nylea watches over all the creatures of the forest except for the snakes. Blessed by Pharika, they can take care of themselves.

"No power is too great to be undone."
—Karametra, god of harvests
Renata led the best hunters in all of Theros on a quest to bring down the terror of the Setessan wilds.

"The first rule of politics can be learned from a lowly hornbeetle: it is wise to cultivate powerful friends."
—Pythamon, sage of Meletis
The Summer Nexus is a holy grove in Setessa where the starfields of Nyx glitter in the shadows.
Where its feet tread, the thunder of many others will follow.
Nature is stillness and savagery in equal measure.
"I bring a wilderness no law can tame."

"A piercing call, bright as the stars, rang out across the valley, calling the Pheres band to war, to blood and savagery."
—Luphea of Setessa, *Histories*
Ancient yet ever-young, it is wise and subtle—and cruel and reckless as the spring itself.
"My time will come, when no road will divide the endless verdure of the trees."
An arrow from Nylea's bow never fails to find its mark.
Calix was patient, steadily following Elspeth until their destined confrontation.

"Far-seeing Kruphix glimpsed the end: Heliod's spear cast down and broken."
—*The Cosmogony*
"A blessing is not a gift. It is a duty."
"Cypress leaves for family, larkspur for protection, amaranth for a bountiful harvest."
Bassara, the tower of the fox, houses the elite skirmishers who guard the Nessian Wood against trespassers.
In the heart of Setessa, the warriors of Leina Tower defend the polis and train its daughters.
"From the ashes of last night's revel, I bring the dawn of new growth."
A typhon's escape from the Underworld makes armies flee and kingdoms fall.
The best healers are intimately familiar with death.
The light of hope blinded Pantor to the ills of the world.
His imagination soars from the depths of the sea to the heights of the heavens.
It slips silently through the still waters of the Labyrinth of Memories to feed.
Nylea speaks to her in the windblown leaves; Thassa in the rushing tides.
"There's no success like excess!"
"Many have sought my weakness. All have failed."
Heroic deeds inspire new heroes.
Three sharp barks announce an attempt to escape the Underworld. Three sharp bites end it.
Some curiosities are best left alone.
A hero dies, and a legend arises.
"Mogis is pleased by this offering. Bring him more!"

"Only cowards flee from the truth."
—Perisophia the philosopher
"Strength, skill, rage—all have their limits, but patience can be infinite."
Every strike of the smith's hammer infuses a sword with the determination of its creator.
Its strings are wayward threads of fate.
A weapon of darkness for a warrior of light.
Meletian mages can't claim the title of thaumaturge until they have received a gift or omen from the gods. Ephara likes to give tangible tokens of her favor.
In times of conflict, the philosophers of Meletis trade their podiums for conveyances of war.
A vision of home, and a glimpse of hope.
Dalakos's invention worked . . . until it didn't.
For centuries, the minotaur polis of Skophos was unknown to humans. It remains unexplored.

"Callaphe gazed on the coastline,
certain her destiny called her
here, where the mist-shrouded rocks sang,
promising glories undreamed of."
—*The Callapheia*

"Agios was felled by a minotaur's blade, but I swear I have seen him since—in the midst of battle, wherever help is needed most."
—Phrokos, soldier of Akros
"For her, I would gladly die again."
"Even in her absence, the light Elspeth kindled in our hearts never faltered."
Ashiok's minions plumb the depths of the ocean and the psyche.
Harpies are among the most detested creatures in all of Theros... and they thoroughly deserve it.
"Every dream is a doorway."
Mirinthes thought death was seconds away when the giant's fist closed around him. Two days later, he was praying for death's release.
Her paean is the clash of spears, her prayer a battle cry.
Riddles draw you in, paradoxes hold you fast, and answers shatter your perceptions.

"Gleams like moonlight on water drew us through the storm and toward our doom."
—Siona, captain of the *Pyleas*
Hatred is a potent ally, but an insatiable master.
Deathless soldiers called phylaskia guard the borders of the Underworld.
Deathbellow Canyon echoes with the roars of minotaurs calling each other to battle.
The forge of Purphoros burns in the heart of Mount Velus, attracting dragons with its blistering heat.

"Put down your bows, you fools! Arrows only make it angry!"
—Callia, Hyrax Tower scout
The wisdom of the past is written on the bones of ancients.
Her webs, spun from her own hair, reach from Nyx to the mortal world and even into the Underworld.

"Dawn-kissed, he nourishes the golden grain."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet
A sip of recollection, an ocean of regrets.
"Right now, in these first moments of creation, it is simultaneously nothing and everything."

They buried Thorin deep beneath the Mountain, and Bard laid the Arkenstone upon his breast. "There let it lie till the Mountain falls!" he said. "May it bring good fortune to all his folk that dwell here after!"
It's never good to walk into an ambush, but with the right spell you might walk out again.

"It is hope, hooved and winged."
—Cymede, queen of Akros

"Training and studies aid a soldier in meager amounts. The gods do the rest."
—Brigone, soldier of Meletis

"The people of Akros must learn from our leonin adversaries. If we match their staunch ferocity with our superior faith, we cannot fail."
—Cymede, queen of Akros
The awards and medals of polis-dwellers mean nothing to griffins, but they repay acts of generosity.
The last thing to go through the cyclops's mind was a twelve-ton block of marble.
"When you threaten the sanctity of the polis, you insult Ephara herself. If she doesn't smite you, I will."
"You. Poet. Be sure to write this down."
No foe is more hated than the former friend.
Honor the gods of Theros, and they will return the favor.
"The best lessons are not the ones I teach. They are the ones the pupils realize for themselves."
In time, all things turn to dust. Some things just take less time.
Formerly oppressed by the polis of Meletis, leonin occasionally "mistake" their old enemies for game.
His soldiers etch his words on the insides of their shields, their inspiration always in sight during battle.
The works of one god last only as long as the patience of another.
She asks pointed questions of the dead who wait for Athreos, learning of life from those who are about to leave it.
"Your god teaches you only how to kill. Karametra teaches me to defend what I hold dear. That is why I will prevail."
Most griffins must be caught and broken into the service of the polis. Not so in Setessa, where they volunteer.

On the fourth day they passed through a forest of immense stacked stones. Althemone, youngest of the companions, called these pillars the work of a god, but the Champion knew better. She quickened her pace.
—*The Theriad*
"I hear the gods' voices in my dreams each night, and I offer bloody trophies on their altars each day."
Legend speaks of the Sun Spear, the mighty weapon that can strike any point in Theros, even the depths of the Underworld.

The Champion and the philosopher Olexa returned from the opposing camp at dusk. Behind them, the enemy raised sail and departed, breaking the siege. When asked what the two had done, the Champion replied, "We spoke to them."
—*The Theriad*
Trust is the only bridle a pegasus will accept.

It was in fields of grain, not fields of battle, that the Champion learned to bear the yoke of duty to the gods. She worked the land long before she was called on to defend it.
—*The Theriad*

"Why pray to the gods, who feed on your worship? Dissolve your illusions and see the true nature of things."
—Xenagos, the Reveler

"Some fates you can see coming for you, plain as day, and there's nothing you can do about them."
—Callaphe the mariner
The wills of mortals shift as the tide ebbs and flows.
Don't try to ride this steed unless you've got gills too.
Seeing a chimera overhead foretells good fortune, but only because seeing one any closer foretells dismemberment.
He calls upon both the currents in the sea and the current in the clouds.
Another imminent battle subsided in busy snuffling and carefree rooting.
"You thought only the gods could stop you?"
The tale of her life was already written, but that didn't mean she could predict the ending.

"You dryfolk must take the air for granted. You constantly insist on wasting it."
—Kenessos, priest of Thassa
When the sea god Thassa wishes to speak with a mortal, she does not issue a summons or grant a vision requesting a visit. The sea simply brings her guest before her.
Even those who leave the labyrinth never escape it, forever dreaming of their time trapped within.
"Every object has an echo in the Æther beyond the world. Every idea has a shadow that can be brought to light."

"It augments anamnesis. What is so confusing about that?"
—Perisophia the philosopher
Her prophecies amaze her even as she speaks them.

"What has neither mouth nor throat, yet swallows captain, crew, and boat?"
—Sphinx's riddle
When a god's will is against you, the day never ends well.

"The most enlightened mages create beauty from violence."
—Medomai the Ageless

"Was this gift cast adrift for any to find, or did Thassa guide the currents to bring it to me alone?"
—Kenessos, priest of Thassa
"Thassa has blessed me with power and insight. I am careful not to disappoint her."

At sunrise, the Champion and her companions awoke to find their supplies gone and Brygus, their sentry, dead. Carefully arranged piles of ornamental shells gave a clear warning: go no further.
—*The Theriad*

"Mists are carefree. They drift where they will, unencumbered by rocks and river beds."
—Thrasios, triton hero
Philosophers say those lost at sea ascended to a more perfect realm. Sailors say they drowned.
"You are breathing borrowed air."
He killed out of hate, so now only hate sustains him. He sought immortality, so the gods gave it to him.
When harpies demand a toll to cross through their territory, consider yourself lucky if they permit payment in coin.

"Death is not a certainty. Erebos determines when a mortal's time is up."
—Iadorna, death priest of Erebos
"Our ambition drives us forward. Together we will claim what is ours, no matter who holds it."

"You're just like me: ruthless, cunning, and ambitious. Obviously you're a threat."
—Basarios the Blade

With spear held high, the Champion came to meet Thyrogog of the Ashlands, who wore the old king's skin as a cloak and fed on the flesh of innocents. The foul minotaur raised the great axe called Goremaster and charged.
—*The Theriad*
More disturbing than the unknown is a distortion of the familiar.
Destiny exalts a chosen few, but even heroes break.
Gold coin, battered helmet, broken wrist bone—all have the same value in the eyes of a harpy.

"No matter who their fickle hearts worship, all mortals belong to one god in the end."
—Iadorna, death priest of Erebos
The Returned have no memory of the Underworld or of their former lives. The golden masks they wear are the last gifts of the selves they left behind.

"The venom cleanses the sickness from your body, but it will not be pleasant, and you may not survive. Pharika's blessings are fickle."
—Solon, acolyte of Pharika
The dead know lessons the living haven't learned.
Driven away by his living kin, he wanders mourning through the wilderness, seeking the dead city of Asphodel.
They lived in different nations and fought in different eras, but as the Returned, they link arms as one.
To members of the cult of Erebos, gold-infused tattoos symbolize the inevitable grasp of the god of death.
Conspirators poisoned the oracle not because her visions were wrong, but because they were right.

"Knowledge is such a burden. Release it. Release all your fears to me."
—Ashiok, Nightmare Weaver

"I could heal a snakebite. Looks like you got bitten by a constellation."
—Aescalos, healer of Pharika
An Akroan soldier's worth is measured by the number of swords raised by his battle cry.
There was no reason to pray. This was already an act of the gods.
The Iroan Games award no medals. Athletes vie for a visit from Iroas, god of victory.

"You have led us to triumph over the forces of Mogis!" said Brygus the Brave, clapping the Champion on the back. The Champion wiped the sweat and blood from her brow. "I count eight graves," she said. "Too many to call this a victory."
—*The Theriad*

"Defeating the Meletians was not so difficult. I needed only to move a mountain."
—Eocles, oracle of Purphoros
It's hard to shout "Shields up!" with a javelin in your chest.

"The temple has been rededicated. It belongs to Mogis now."
—Rastos, disciple of Mogis

"When fire is shackled to candle and torch, subjected to insignificance, it finds a way to lash out at its masters."
—Vala, disciple of Purphoros
Attending a satyr revel requires a high tolerance for pain.
"I see your future, mantled in ash."
All the world is Purphoros's anvil.
A cyclops has two moods: angry and asleep.
"It used to be a lair. Now it's just a tunnel."

"The hand of Keranos can be seen in every rumbling storm cloud. Best not to stand where he points."
—Rakleia of Shrine Peak

"He outran arrows. He outran even the archers' insults."
—Bayma, storyteller of Lagonna Band

"Their only dreams are of full stomachs."
—Kleon the Iron-Booted

"Early olive buds? A good omen. Flock of crows? Not so good. Mountain exploding? Bad. Very, very bad."
—Hira, street oracle
"Even my last breath will be a blow struck for Iroas."

"I see a spark of pure rage. Soon that spark will spread from the depths of Kragma. Soon its fire will engulf the polis."
—Hira, street oracle
A satyr is bound by nothing—not home, not family, not loyalty.
Acolytes of Purphoros hammer the world until they see the sparks of change.
There is no gift more precious or more perilous than fire.
The left head keeps the right head starved as motivation to track new prey.
"You can tell something's really valuable by the sound it makes when you slam your staff into it."
The light in the woods just before dawn reveals a glimmering network of branches, roots, and spiderwebs. The acolytes of Kruphix walk this lattice unseen.
The warriors she leads can rarely keep pace with her, and neither can the tales.
Some seers read bones or entrails. Others just like to break things.

"A herd is only as strong as its weakest. Our weakest just killed his third minotaur raider—today."
—Braulios of Pheres Band
For the first time in many years, Elspeth asked for help.
The defenders said not a word. Their shields, spears, and stances were warning enough.

"Are the gods angry at our discontent with what they give us, or jealous that we made a thing they cannot?"
—Kleon the Iron-Booted
Nylea's sacred lynx guards those who honor the Nessian Wood and hunts those who don't.

"A grudge is a tattoo worn on the inside."
—Setessan warrior saying
"The wilds are a garden tended by divine hands."
It's not the two heads you should fear. It's the four fangs.

Khestes the Adamant, the Champion's closest ally among the centaurs, took one stone to his shoulder and another to his flank. He held his stride and his aim, and let fly the arrow that killed the giant Grinthax.
—*The Theriad*

"Poets speak of your unrivaled speed," the Champion said to the assembled centaurs, "but it is plain to see that your true strength lies in your unwavering loyalty to one another."
—*The Theriad*
"Any festival you can walk away from wasn't worth attending in the first place."

"When I asked my commander the reward for killing that prancing nuisance, he told me, 'None! I want to kill him myself!'"
—Phrogas, soldier of Akros

"I thought its back was turned!"
"A centaur has two backs!"

Thakolides the Mighty
Slayer of minotaurs
Vanquisher of giants
Killed by a scorpion
—Inscription on an Akroan grave

"Enemies of the wood! Your presence here is a slap in Nylea's face. Do not be surprised if she slaps back."
—Telphe, druid of Nylea
As soon as she faces a monster, she begins composing its epitaph.
Those who enter the copse never leave. They find peace there and take root, becoming part of the ever-growing grove.
"None can own the land's bounty. The gods made this world for all to share its riches. And I'm not just saying that because you caught me stealing your fruit."

"With a diet of hydras, giants, and massive serpents, anything would get that big."
—Corisande, Setessan hunter

"Let each challenge make you a better warrior."
—Anthousa of Setessa
"Fair fight? How could it be a fair fight? We're Akroans. They're not."
Akros's greatest heroes are also its royalty.
One offering to appease her on her arrival. Another to celebrate her departure.
